 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender

entities.text: Gajji Seethamma vs Sardar Jagir Singh And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award dated 12.09.2008 in O.P.No.798 of 2005 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (District Judge) at Khammam, the claimant has preferred this appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (District Judge) at Khammam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard both sides and perused the entire material on record.
3.
The claimant is wife of deceased.
She has filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- and the Tribunal has granted Rs.6,01,216/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization.

4. According to version of the claimant, on 29.06.1999, while the deceased was going on TVS Suziki motorcycle, the offending vehicle which is a lorry driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner hit the motorcycle, resulting in grievous injuries all over the body to the deceased.
Subsequently, he had undergone treatment in various hospitals and on 29.04.2000, he succumbed to injuries.
KS, J MACMA_450_2010 5.
Admittedly, the deceased was working as Government Teacher.
Ex.A11 Last Pay certificate shows the monthly gross salary of deceased as Rs.8,898/- without standard deductions.
The employer of the deceased who was examined as RW2 stated that after the revision of pay scales, the gross salary of the deceased as on the date of accident became Rs.11,843/-.
The learned Tribunal has taken the net salary of the deceased as Rs.9,038/- after deducting standard deductions at Rs.2,805/- and granted compensation.

Hence, this Court is inclined to take the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.11,843/- and grant compensation.
6.
The age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 54 years.

Relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1, if 15 percent of the income is included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.13,619/- (Rs.11,843+1,776).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If 1/3rd of the income is deducted towards personal expenditure, as per the authority in Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2, thus the annual 2017 (6) 170 (SC) (2009) 6 S.C.C. 121 KS,
J MACMA_450_2010 contribution of the deceased to the claimant would be Rs.1,08,948/-
(Rs.13,619-4,540X12).

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Schedule II of the Act, if the said annual contribution arrived is multiplied with relevant multiplier to the age of the deceased i.e. '11', the total amount comes to Rs.11,98,428/-.
The claimant is entitled for the said amount under the head of loss of dependency.

sentences.text: Further, under the conventional heads, the Tribunal has granted meager amounts.
Relying on the ratio laid down in case of Pranay Sethi (1 supra), the claimant is granted Rs.30,000/- towards funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Further, the claimant is granted Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium.
8. The death of the deceased is consequence of injuries sustained in the accident.
Admittedly, the deceased has taken treatment after the accident for a long time.
Considering the medical bills under Ex.A7, the Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head of medical expenses and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding.
KS, J MACMA_450_2010 9.

Therefore, the claimant is eligible for the compensation as below:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.11,98,428/-
 (2) Funeral expenses and Loss of Estate Rs.30,000  (3) Spousal consortium Rs.40,000  (4) Medical expenses Rs.3,00,000

Total compensation awarded Rs.15,68,428/-
10.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.6,01,216/- to Rs.15,68,428/-.
(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The claimant shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation (c) The respondents shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.

On such deposit, claimant is entitled to KS, J MACMA_450_2010 withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

K.SURENDER, J Date : 12.08.2024 gvl Gajji Seethamma vs Sardar Jagir Singh And Another on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113905253/
